title: The Greatest Common Divisor of a Range, With Changes

concept.title: The gcd of a block is the gcd of the gcds of its two halves, so gcd fits a segment tree just like a sum
body: A row of positive numbers changes one cell at a time, and questions ask for the **greatest common divisor** of all the numbers from `x` to `y`. For `12 18 30 8` the gcd of the cells 1 to 3 is 6, and of all four cells it is 2. Subtracting does not work for the gcd (there is no inverse), so prefix tables cannot be used after changes.

The gcd is **associative**: `gcd(a, b, c, d) = gcd(gcd(a, b), gcd(c, d))`, and `gcd(0, x) = x`, so 0 is a neutral element. Therefore the segment tree works exactly as for the minimum, with `gcd` as the combining operation and 0 as the value of unused leaves. A change recomputes the gcds of the parents of one leaf; a question combines the gcds of O(log n) blocks.

One gcd costs O(log 10^9) steps (about 45 divisions in the worst case), but the gcds of nearby blocks share a lot of structure, so the total cost per change or question is O(log n + log max) in amortised terms, which is fast enough for 30000 operations. This structure is also a good example of a tree that is not a sum.

statement: A row of `n` positive numbers is given. Process `q` operations: type 1 `x y` sets the number at the position `x` to `y`; type 2 `x y` asks for the greatest common divisor of the numbers at the positions `x` to `y`. Print the answers to the questions on one line, in order.
inputFormat: The first line has `n` and `q`: the number of cells and the number of operations.
The second line has `n` numbers: the cells.
Each of the next `q` lines has three numbers `t`, `x` and `y`. If `t = 1`, set the cell number `x` to the value `y`. If `t = 2`, print the greatest common divisor of the cells `x` to `y`.
outputFormat: Print one number for every operation of type 2, separated by spaces.
constraints: Cells are numbered from 1; for a question 1 <= x <= y <= n.
hints: gcd is associative and gcd(0, x) = x.
Use the same tree as for the minimum, with gcd as the operation.

explanation: A segment tree with gcd as the combining operation (0 for unused leaves) supports changing one cell and the gcd of a range in O(log n) combinations.
solution.complexity: Time O((n + q) (log n + log max)), space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

def gcd(a, b):
    while b:
        a, b = b, a % b
    return a

n, q = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
ops = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(q)]

size = 1
while size < n:
    size *= 2
tree = [0] * (2 * size)
for i in range(n):
    tree[size + i] = a[i]
for v in range(size - 1, 0, -1):
    tree[v] = gcd(tree[2 * v], tree[2 * v + 1])
out = []
for kind, x, y in ops:
    if kind == 1:
        v = size + x - 1
        tree[v] = y
        v //= 2
        while v:
            tree[v] = gcd(tree[2 * v], tree[2 * v + 1])
            v //= 2
    else:
        lo = size + x - 1
        hi = size + y
        res = 0
        while lo < hi:
            if lo & 1:
                res = gcd(res, tree[lo])
                lo += 1
            if hi & 1:
                hi -= 1
                res = gcd(res, tree[hi])
            lo //= 2
            hi //= 2
        out.append(res)
print(*out)
